A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIALDEFER and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained methods and experiments can be matched reliably across the expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of four LLMs, judgment-flip analyses, speaker-label ablations and mitigation experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds GPT-5-mini evaluations, mitigation experiments on additional models, paraphrase tests and class-balanced analyses.

M1.justification: The paired C1/C2 framework and the Be Honest, Dehumanizing, SFT and DPO procedures are retained. The expanded Dehumanizing description matches v1 Appendix I.1; applying existing interventions to additional judges does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine benchmark datasets plus the 280-instance r/AIO dataset. The abstract's nine-to-ten-domain wording includes already-existing r/AIO coverage. The paraphrase experiments preserve the original task and data.

E2.justification: The matched Qwen mitigation comparison retains baseline C2, Be Honest, Dehumanizing, SFT and DPO. Additional model experiments reuse these interventions. GPT-5-mini is an additional evaluated judge, rather than a competing mitigation method.

E3.justification: v2 adds GPT-5-mini, extends prompting to three judges and fine-tuning to two, and introduces three paraphrase pairs evaluated on all 790 TruthfulQA items for two models. It also introduces OR/NOR-balanced evaluation. Existing per-dataset splits remain unchanged; the benchmark test-count revision from 2,864 to 2,964 corrects the stated total.

E4.justification: New Appendices D and E test whether DDS depends on prompt wording or r/AIO class imbalance, addressing two previously untested explanations. Existing perspective-reversal, speaker-label and reasoning-taxonomy analyses are retained, while cross-model flip consistency is extended from four to five judges.

E5.justification: v2 Table 15 adds means and standard deviations across three paraphrases, measuring variation across templates rather than repeated seeds. Sampling seed 42 and McNemar testing are retained. The GPT-4o-mini GPQA confidence interval previously quoted in the results discussion is omitted.

E6.justification: v2 adds GPT-5-mini outcomes, including 75.6% C1 accuracy, 75.4% C2 accuracy and DDS +8.3 in Table 2, plus additional mitigation and robustness results. Existing entries also change: Qwen's r/AIO Dehumanizing accuracy changes from 55.9% in v1 Table 19 to 45.5% in v2 Table 21, reversing its reported accuracy effect from +6.1 to -4.3 percentage points.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix E introduces the mathematical definition Balanced DDS = (DDS_OR + DDS_NOR)/2. The original DDS definition and SFT/DPO mathematical formulation remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about framing-induced shifts, accuracy masking and calibration remain. The introduction narrows fine-tuning benefits to model-dependent outcomes, claims Dehumanizing is the most stable tested intervention, and explicitly includes the reasoning-failure taxonomy among the contributions.

C2.justification: v1's statement that fine-tuning consistently outperforms prompting becomes Qwen-specific in v2, with Gemma failures changing the mitigation interpretation. v2 also identifies GPT-5-mini's exception to the validation-bias pattern. Conversely, it removes the Model Coverage limitation explaining that training-paradigm effects cannot be disentangled without controlled comparisons.

D1.justification: v2 documents the tested paraphrase wording in Appendix D and adds the GPT-5-mini API identifier in Appendix C.1. Existing Qwen hyperparameters, hardware, training times and release information are retained. Appendix K does not supply corresponding Gemma-specific fine-tuning details.

R1.justification: v2 adds prompt-sensitivity references by Sclar and Mizrahi, persona-prompting references by Tan and Luz de Araujo, and the GPT-5 system card. Section 5.2 newly distinguishes changing the evaluated speaker's attribution from assigning a persona to the judge. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify speaker roles, contributions and mitigation findings. Dataset subsections become numbered, mitigation discussion is incorporated into Section 4, and new appendix sections shift subsequent numbering. The main section order and most existing appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 5 is reorganized from a Qwen-only comparison into three model blocks with separate benchmark and r/AIO DDS columns. Figures 2–5 are revised, detailed result tables expand and reflow, and six paraphrase-prompt figures plus new robustness and mitigation tables are added. The appendix layout also leaves PDF page 31 almost empty.

improvement.justification: The paraphrase and class-balanced checks strengthen validation, while broader mitigation experiments replace v1's overly general fine-tuning conclusion with model-dependent evidence. These gains support a modest net improvement. However, Gemma-specific training details remain undocumented, and v2 changes its r/AIO DDS to 86.4 in Table 20 despite component accuracies implying about 87.1, introducing an internal numerical inconsistency.
